title: `ng-container` element inside an <svg> results in "Template parse errors: ':svg:ng-container' is not a known element"

labels.name: area: core
labels.description: Issues related to the framework runtime

body:
<!--

**Current behavior**
the following template:
```html
<svg>
  <ng-container *ngFor="let item of items">
    <my-graphic-content *ngIf="item.valid" [item]="item"></my-graphic-content>
  </ng-container>
</svg>
```
results in compilation error:
```
Unhandled Promise rejection: Template parse errors:
':svg:ng-container' is not a known element:
1. If ':svg:ng-container' is an Angular component, then verify that it is part of this module.
2. If ':svg:ng-container' is a Web Component then add "CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA" to the '@NgModule.schemas' of this component to suppress this message. 
```

**Expected behavior**
Since <ng-container> doesn't affect the markup and only adds the comments, the expected behavior would be successfull template compilation.

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
See [this plunk](http://plnkr.co/edit/UkZAmrugq0lJ3OKyIPc2?p=preview)

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
Making the process of laying out svg components smoother and bug-free

**Please tell us about your environment:**
npm 4, webpack 2, VSCode, MacOS Sierra
